 Massachusetts Couple Discovers Four Shared Catholic Sacraments
 James Anderson 
 Published 
 Oct 20, 2026 - 19:57 
 2 
 Reads 
 Last Update 
 Oct 20, 2026 - 19:57 
 Share 
 WhatsApp 
 Ryan and Jessica McGinty. Photography by Amanda Curry. 
 Smallest Font 
 Largest Font 
 A Massachusetts couple discovered an unexpected connection spanning their lives after reviewing family records while planning their wedding . Ryan and Jessica McGinty, who grew up in neighboring Westwood and Walpole, learned they had received four Catholic sacraments together at St. Timothy Catholic Church in Norwood: baptism, first communion, confirmation and marriage.
 The discovery revealed that the couple had shared religious milestones long before they met in college. Although they grew up in different towns, had separate friendship circles and attended different colleges, their families had connections to the same parish.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Jessica recalled that Ryan expressed his intentions early in their relationship, after they met during her visit to friends on his college campus.

 "It was junior year of college and he did tell me that we were going to get married the day that he met me," Jessica McGinty recalled, laughing.
 The couple also learned that they had lived remarkably close to each other throughout their childhoods without becoming acquainted.
 "Seven minutes away from each other our whole life and didn't know each other," Jessica said.
 Also Read 
 Lay's Launches Five Thanksgiving Inspired Chip Flavors 
 St. Timothy Catholic Church remained a familiar place for both families. Ryan's father continues to serve as a lector at the Norwood parish, where the couple also attends services.
 "My dad's still a lector here," Ryan McGinty said. "We still come here. This is probably the best place to be because this is where we've been our whole lives."
 The connection became clear during wedding preparations, when the couple's families compared details about their religious histories. Jessica said their mothers remembered that the couple had been baptized on the same day in February, during freezing weather.
 Also Read 
 Citadel Outlets Installs 115 Foot Christmas Tree in Commerce 
 Michelle Gallo, a pastoral associate at the church, examined the parish's registry books and confirmed the shared baptism. She then reviewed the records for the couple's other sacraments.
 "I was looking at the registry books and sure enough they were baptized together," Michelle Gallo said.
 Her review uncovered the additional milestones linking Ryan and Jessica through the church, extending their shared history beyond baptism to their wedding.
 Also Read 
 Shelvy Neal Celebrates Her 80th Birthday With a Living Funeral 
 "I decided to look at the other sacraments, sure enough, first communion, confirmation, and now wedding. What are the odds of that? To think that you were together to receive all those graces four times? That's pretty special," Gallo said.
 The couple said their relationship is supported by their families, their connection to the parish and their mutual respect. Jessica described the reassurance she feels in her husband's affection, including on difficult days.
 "Even when I'm having a bad day, come home from work and I'm maybe in a bad mood, I still feel Ryan's love all the time," Jessica said.

 Ryan also praised his wife's character, describing the positive regard she receives from people who know her.
 "You would have a really hard time with all the people that know her, to find one person that had a bad thing to say about her," her husband said.
